summary: settlement-service stopped consuming because order-service deploy dep-6010 (v2.16.0) renamed the OrderExecuted field `qty`→`quantity` and bumped the schema header to v2, while settlement-service's deserializer still expects schema v1. Every message on orders-3 (offset 8841207) fails deserialization; the consumer enters a poison-message retry loop and the partition is blocked, so zero settlements post and consumer_lag grows monotonically (~45 → 61,605 messages). The config change to max.poll.records (500→200) and the errors are coincidental/adjacent, not causal: a smaller poll batch cannot produce a `missing required field 'qty'` deserialization failure. Resource/infra causes are contradicted by flat db_pool (~6), zero restarts, and flat HTTP error_rate. Fix is to restore schema compatibility (roll back dep-6010 or make settlement-service tolerate v2 / skip the poison offset).

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2 schema deploy broke settlement-service deserializer
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deploy dep-6010 (order-service v2.16.0) renamed OrderExecuted field qty->quantity and stamped header v2; settlement-service still expects schema v1, so every message fails to deserialize, the consumer loops on a poison offset and blocks partition 3, halting all settlements and growing lag.

causal_chain.claim: dep-6010 renames qty->quantity and sets header v2 at 07:40
settlement-service deserializer expects v1 -> missing required field 'qty' errors from 07:42:14
consumer retries the same offset, blocking partition 3 (poison message)
zero settlements posted and consumer_lag grows monotonically

assumptions: settlement-service deserializer was not updated to accept v2 in the same window (no such deploy/config observed)
orders-3@8841207 is the first failed offset and blocks the partition head

ranked_hypotheses.title: Consumer poll-settings config change throttled consumption
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-3004 lowered consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 on settlement-service at 07:35, reducing throughput enough to cause lag and stalls.
assumptions: throughput reduction alone could stall settlements
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: A smaller poll batch cannot produce 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' deserialization errors or block a partition; lag growth is fully explained by the poison-message loop after the 07:40 deploy.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka broker rebalance / partition reassignment (per historical pattern)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A broker-side rebalance caused settlement-service to lose its partition assignment, letting lag grow and settlements stall, as in HIST-104/HIST-112.
assumptions: a rebalance occurred but was not logged
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No rebalance/reassignment evidence; restarts=0, and the consumer is actively processing (thousands of retry attempts on a specific offset), which is inconsistent with a lost assignment.

facts.statement: order-service deploy dep-6010 (v2.16.0) at 07:40:00Z renamed the OrderExecuted field qty->quantity and set event schema header v2.
settlement-service began emitting 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' deserialization errors at 07:42:14Z, ~2 minutes after dep-6010.
settlement-service entered a poison-message retry loop that blocked partition 3 (orders-3@8841207).
settlement-service consumer_lag grew from ~45 to 61,605.53 messages, with onset in the 07:36-07:48 window.
The only config change was consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 on settlement-service at 07:35:00Z.
settlement-service db_pool_in_use stayed flat at ~6 connections, restarts=0, and HTTP error_rate stayed ~0.2% throughout, ruling out DB exhaustion, restarts, and HTTP-level saturation.
order-service logged no relevant errors in the window (one unrelated slow-request WARN).
Prior similar incidents were attributed to Kafka rebalance/partition reassignment, a different cause than the schema mismatch observed here.

assumptions: settlement-service was not simultaneously updated to accept schema v2 (no such deploy/config appeared in the window).
orders-3@8841207 is the head/blocking poison offset on partition 3.
Kafka broker health was normal; no rebalance was captured in the searched windows.

timeline.event: Deploy dep-6010: order-service v2.16.0 renames OrderExecuted field qty->quantity, header v2.
First settlement-service deserialization error (missing required field 'qty').
Poison-message retry loop begins; partition orders-3 blocked.
Incident INC-010 reported (no settlements for ~40 min, lag >60k).

recommended_actions.action: Roll back order-service dep-6010 to the previous version (or emit v1-compatible OrderExecuted with qty) to stop producing v2 messages.
recommended_actions.rationale: The v2 schema change is the trigger; halting new incompatible events stops the error stream.

recommended_actions.action: Make settlement-service skip or dead-letter the poison offset orders-3@8841207 to unblock partition 3, then replay after the schema fix.
recommended_actions.rationale: The retry loop on a blocked partition is why zero settlements post; unblocking restores consumption.

recommended_actions.action: Add schema-compatibility (backward-compatible) deserialization or a v2 handler for OrderExecuted in settlement-service.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents producer schema evolution from wedging the consumer.

recommended_actions.action: Add a bounded retry + dead-letter path so a single unparseable message cannot block a whole partition.
recommended_actions.rationale: The poison-message partition block amplified one bad message into a full outage.

recommended_actions.action: Introduce contract/schema-registry gating in CI for order-service event schema changes.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents incompatible field renames from reaching consumers.

data_gaps: No direct Kafka broker-side telemetry (rebalance/partition-assignment events) was queried; broker health is inferred from absence of rebalance evidence and restarts=0.
The settlement-service logs were truncated (409 total matches, 40 returned), so the full set of distinct failing offsets/patterns was not enumerated - all sampled errors are the same qty/v2 pattern.
No deployment of settlement-service itself was observed, so it is assumed its deserializer was unchanged.

findings.statement: order-service deploy dep-6010 (v2.16.0) landed at 07:40:00Z and renamed the OrderExecuted field qty->quantity with an event schema version header v2.

The first settlement-service deserialization ERROR appears at 07:42:14Z, ~2 min after dep-6010, matching 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted ... missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' (213 occurrences).

refs.quote: failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)

findings.statement: settlement-service then enters a poison-message retry loop on the same offset, blocking the partition: 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt <n>), partition blocked' (196 occurrences).

refs.quote: poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 92490), partition blocked

findings.statement: consumer_lag was flat ~40-65 messages until the 07:36 bucket, then grew from 774.71 to 61,605.53 by 09:48, i.e. onset in the 07:36-07:48 window.
The only config change was on settlement-service at 07:35:00Z: consumer.max.poll.records 500 -> 200 ('Smaller poll batches to smooth DB writes').
settlement-service db_pool_in_use stayed flat around 6 connections (mean 6.0) throughout the incident - no DB connection exhaustion.
settlement-service restarts metric was 0 across every bucket - no process/broker-driven restart.
settlement-service HTTP error_rate stayed ~0.2% flat and CPU rose from ~28% to ~70% starting the 07:36 bucket, tracking the retry loop rather than a saturation event.
order-service emitted no relevant errors in this window (only a single unrelated slow-request WARN at 09:14:44Z), consistent with the broker/consumer side being where the failure surfaces.
Prior similar incidents (HIST-104, HIST-112) were Kafka broker rebalance/partition-reassignment failures, not schema mismatches - similar symptoms but a different proposed cause.

refs.quote: Consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance

findings.statement: The poison-message loop is the mechanism that converts a per-message deserialization failure into a full partition block (zero settlements) and unbounded lag growth.
